Another Search and Seizure a Year After Fatal Fall... Legal Risks Hit GS E&C GS E&C was recently subjected to a search and seizure of its headquarters by the Ministry of Employment and Labor and police in connection with the death of a construction-site worker last year. The move has been described as unusual, as authorities launched a forced investigation targeting the headquarters more than a year after the accident. Attention is focused on whether charges will be brought. According to reporting by The Asia Business Daily on November 4, the Ministry of Employment and Labor and police recently searched and seized materials at GS E&C's headquarters in Grand Seoul, Jongno-gu, Seoul. An official from the ministry said, "We conducted the search and seizure jointly with the police to prove the allegations of violating the Serious Accidents Punishment Act." The investigation concerns a fatal fall at the Cheonggye Riverview Xi construction site in Yongdap-dong, Seongdong-gu, Seoul, in September last year. At the time, a subcontractor's worker in his 50s, identified as Mr. A, fell from the height of the 15th floor of an apartment building while dismantling large formwork and died. People in the construction industry said the timing of the search and seizure at the headquarters was somewhat unusual. Although authorities had already conducted a forced investigation of the site office and other locations last year, shortly after the accident, they directly searched the company's headquarters more than a year later. Cheonggye Riverview Xi is scheduled to welcome residents in February next year. The possibilities have narrowed to a few. After conducting the investigation for about a year, authorities may have identified evidence they had not previously obtained, or uncovered additional clues through tips implicating headquarters executives, including the chief safety officer. Given the time that has passed, the court would have had to scrutinize the requirements for issuing a warrant more carefully. The fact that a forced investigation was carried out suggests that there was something additional to examine. If so, the possibility that executives at GS E&C, the principal contractor, will be indicted may have increased. GS E&C President Kim Taejin oversees safety as chief safety strategy officer (CSSO). However, the search and seizure may also have been prompted by limited progress in the investigation to date, or by the Public Prosecution Office requesting further investigation after receiving the case records. With investigative and prosecution duties previously handled by prosecutors now separated, and the division of responsibilities still unclear, the repercussions could be significant if executives are brought to trial on charges of violating the Serious Accidents Punishment Act over an accident at a site where GS E&C was the principal contractor. At the time of last year's accident that prompted this forced investigation, CEO Yoon Hong Huh apologized to the public and promised measures to prevent a recurrence. Goldman has three operating segments: Asset & Wealth Management, Global Banking & Markets, and Platform Solutions, with the latter including transaction banking and consumer partnerships. 10 Questions About Artificial Intelligence: Part 2 Artificial intelligence (AI) has been and remains one of the fastest-growing technology developments in history. Just a few years after becoming broadly known, AI represents a significant portion of the global economy and is now the preeminent focus among investors. Developments in AI have progressed and continue to unfold rapidly, and new revelations on one day - say, the release of Meta Platforms Inc.'s Muse model - can make preconceptions about AI seem out of date.  Based on input from clients, investors, industry experts, and our own analytic team, Argus has put together what we see as 10 current key and enduring questions about AI, along with our responses. We've broken these 10 questions into Parts 1, 2, and 3.  Part 2, presented below, addresses three key questions including risks that white-hot growth at the GPU makers might slow, key adjacencies benefiting from AI infrastructure build-outs, and a discussion of companies best and worst-positioned amid AI disruption. Following publication of Part 2, we will be publishing Parts 3. We welcome feedback from clients and will continue to refine our 10 questions about AI in real time in response to this exciting and ever-changing opportunity.  QUESTION 4: At the heart of the artificial intelligence (AI) revolution are the graphics processing unit (GPU) developers, led by Nvidia Corp. and Advanced Micro Devices Inc. and followed by a host of others. What is the risk that these companies' white-hot growth slows or stops? ANSWER 4: AI infrastructure investment has broadened out from an initial focus on hyperscaler data centers to a broader set of customers, including enterprises, sovereigns, and neoclouds. Wider adoption is being driven by the much more diverse range of use cases driven by agentic AI. This broadening of the market has benefited the makers of GPUs, which represent the foundational piece in massive clusters required for model training, deep learning, and inference. Nvidia is the tentpole company of the AI revolution, initially repurposing its GPU gaming cards for early AI tasks. The company was also subject to fluctuations in the crypto market and consumer cycles in gaming demand. Nvidia's revenue declined 7% in fiscal 2020, rebounded to mid-50% annual growth in FY21 and FY22, and was flat in FY23 on softening in crypto and consumer end markets. After two years of triple-digit growth in FY24 and FY25, growth moderated to 6% in FY26 before reaccelerating to 87% in the January 2027 fiscal year. Although growth is on a path to 'moderate' to the 70% range in FY28, note that growth in dollars remains robust: rising from $216 billion in FY26 to an estimated $410 billion in FY27 and to $680 billion in FY28, according to the consensus. If not for supply constraints, according to CEO Jensen Huang, FY28 top-line growth would be meaningfully higher. Nvidia has teamed up with Wall Street giants (Apollo Global Management Inc., Blackrock Inc., Goldman Sachs Group Inc., and others) to raise $500 billion in capital for AI infrastructure. Nvidia anticipates multiple years of strong growth ahead. AMD is No. 2 in GPUs and is also benefiting as inference drives demand for industry standard servers (ISSs) using AMD's central processing units (CPUs). AMD generated $6.6 billion in revenue in 2010 but did not get back above that number until 2019. After three years of mid-double-digit growth in 2020-22, revenue declined in 2023 and grew 14% in 2024. Fueled by both its CPU and GPU franchises, growth accelerated to 34% in 2025 and is on a path to accelerate from 47% in 2026 to 73% in 2027. In dollar terms, AMD's revenue is forecast to rise from $35 billion in 2025 to $51 billion in 2026 and $88 billion in 2027. Companies including Broadcom Inc. and Marvell Technology Inc., which make application accelerators and XPUs (both of which are task-specific GPUs), are reporting similar growth trajectories as customer and market opportunities broaden. AI infrastructure spending grew about 60% annually to $320 billion in 2025, according to industry analysis firm IDC. AI infrastructure spending is on a path to exceed $1 trillion in 2029, the firm estimates. IDC noted that AI infrastructure investment is accelerating at a pace that signals a clear shift away from experimentation to a sustained, multiyear capital commitment cycle by end customers. Based on these and other forecasts and guidance from the major GPU providers, we expect GPU and related semiconductor growth to sustain and in many cases accelerate from high levels in coming years. QUESTION 5: What are some the key adjacencies that are benefiting from AI development? And which of these companies are best positioned to thrive? ANSWER 5: The initial gold-rush phase of AI was characterized by intense activity among hyperscalers to build massive GPU clusters and support infrastructure as they sought to develop and train their own large language models (LLMs). But this focus on AI data centers also represented one of the key bottlenecks in AI infrastructure. AI content, in the words of rock singer Meat Loaf, was 'all revved up with no place to go.' Late in 2024 and early in 2025, Argus noted that the AI revolution had primarily been focused within hyperscalers (major cloud service providers) and was concentrated in GPU compute at massive cloud data centers. Argus forecast that in coming years, the AI revolution would spread out from this initial concentration at hyperscalers to include customers in other categories including major enterprises, sovereigns, and neoclouds. We further forecast that the need to accommodate AI-generated data would trigger massive business growth at data storage and memory companies. And we forecast that the need to disseminate AI data to these new classes of customers would trigger massive business growth at data networking companies.  Those forecasts began to play out during 2025, as data storage and memory companies had huge business growth and were among the best stocks in the S&P 500. During 2026, data networking companies have reported strong double-digit growth rates, and their stocks are leading the Information Technology sector and broad market. The first phase of generative AI, dominated by the training of LLMs, is giving way to the age of agentic and physical AI, which requires much more compute-intensive inference in multimodal and frontier models. This is further contributing to AI-related data growth.  Technology segments benefiting from the need to deliver AI-as-a-system include data storage and memory, networking, and traditional enterprise infrastructure. In these segments, Argus has identified multiple companies best positioned to benefit from the broadening in AI demand. In the networking space, Argus favors optical-networking leader Ciena Corp., 'cloud titan' network provider Arista Networks Inc., and enterprise industry leader Cisco Systems Inc. as three companies well positioned to deliver AI services to customers. In the data storage and memory space, Argus favors Seagate Technology Holdings plc and Western Digital Corp., which form a duopoly in nearline hard disk drives for AI data centers; Sandisk Corp. in the nonvolatile memory space; and Micron Technology Inc., the leading U.S.-based provider of DRAM and NAND memory. Data storage systems providers including NetApp Inc. are subject to higher input costs for their solutions, but NetApp has driven revenue acceleration with successful cost pass-alongs and higher prices.  Dell Technologies Inc. is a good example of the fast-developing market opportunity in the legacy enterprise infrastructure space. As of mid-2026, Dell had thousands of customers for its AI servers and related IT infrastructure including storage arrays, industry standard servers, and networking gear. None of these customers included the major hyperscalers.  As of August 2026, Dell expected at least $74 billion in AI-optimized server revenue in FY27, almost triple the $25 billion in FY26. Dell's traditional x86-based ISS revenue grew more than 120% annually in the most recent quarter. In 1H27, Dell generated as much revenue from ISS and networking than it generated in any full prior year in company history.  Outside the Information Technology sector, industrial companies providing power, cooling, electrical, and related solutions are also experiencing extraordinary growth. Top beneficiaries include Caterpillar Inc., Emerson Electric Co., Honeywell International Inc., Rockwell Automation Inc., and others. As AI demand continues to broaden out, we expect strong and even accelerated growth for providers of the adjacent infrastructure enabling the AI revolution.   QUESTION 6: Which incumbents are most vulnerable to AI disruption? And which are best positioned to integrate AI defensively? ANSWER 6: The AI revolution has been so consistently strong and inclusive that it initially swept along much of the Information Technology sector. But as the AI revolution moves beyond year three, several significant developments have revealed risks to industry incumbents across the technology landscape. These developments primarily relate to AI displacement and the impact of soaring component costs in a supply-constrained environment. Fears of AI displacement have been mainly centered in the enterprise application software space. The trajectory of these fears is expressed in the iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF (IGV). The software ETF hit an all-time closing high around 117 in September 2025. The release of certain highly capable frontier models, most notably Anthropic PBC's Claude Code, showed that many formerly proprietary software tasks could be done quickly and cheaply with AI. IGV declined gradually into year-end 2025 and then its decline accelerated in the new year, reaching bottom at a closing low of 74 in April 2026. IGV has since rebounded to a low-100s level, as software companies counter displacement fears by highlighting their proprietary products, deep customer engagements, and defense against 'weakest link' cybersecurity vulnerabilities. Component prices and particularly memory prices have soared due to voracious hyperscaler appetites for hardware to support infrastructure investment. Companies with high personal computer exposure such as HP Inc. report that memory is now up to 70% of the bill of materials cost of building a PC. In releasing its newest iPhone family in September 2026, Apple Inc. raised iPhone prices by approximately $100 per device and more for high-memory-content phones. These rising costs and the urgency to invest in AI are causing chief information officers to reshape their IT budgets in some cases away from long-standing customers.  International Business Machines Corp., which in April 2026 warned of a decline in 2Q26 infrastructure revenue, reported a steeper-than-expected demand decline in July 2026. Customers shifted purchases away from IBM's mainframe computers and its complementary transactional software stack. These customers redirected spending to ISS servers, a market in which IBM no longer competes, and data storage in order to secure supply-constrained IT hardware ahead of further price increases. IBM shares declined sharply on the 2Q26 revenue miss and are down 22% year-to-date. But the stock is up sharply from pre-AI days. IBM Watson playing Jeopardy against a past champion helped popularize the concept of AI years before ChatGPT. IBM, like the software companies and makers of AI PCs, should ultimately benefit from positioning within the AI ecosystem. We expect creative disruption to continue to challenge industry incumbents.  As to which companies are best positioned to integrate AI defensively, no company is in a position to sit on the sidelines and watch its competitors bring AI practices into their everyday operations and into customer interactions. Market sectors at the forefront of AI adoption, for both offensive and defensive reasons, include Healthcare, Information Technology, and Financial. Even in regulated sectors such as Utilities, which would seem to have less urgency to integrate AI into their operations, sector companies are adding smart meter technology and using AI to upgrade their internal operations. In short, nearly every company inside and outside of the AI ecosystem will need to integrate AI both offensively and defensively. Lexus recorded those figures with prototypes of the 300-hp V8 version of the second-generation Lexus GS. Not bad for a car dressed for a board meeting. Yet buyers often chase its Supra-related inline-six, which made 225 hp, or mistake it for the V6-powered ES 300. The engine with the bigger reputation might not be the better used-car buy. Under the GS 300's hood, six pistons rise and fall in one long row, with 24 valves controlling how the engine breathes. This 3.0-liter 2JZ-GE made 225 hp and 220 lb-ft in 1998, driving the rear wheels through an automatic. But the Supra family connection doesn't include the turbocharged Supra's hardware, and chasing that extra power means building a turbo car, not unlocking a factory secret. There's another trap under the Lexus badge. The ES 300's 1MZ-FE is a V6 mounted sideways for front-wheel drive. The GS 300 has a straight-six stretching lengthwise, with power going rearward. Open their hoods and the layout tells two different stories. Even service access changes; an ES repair complaint isn't evidence against the GS.In Japan, the second-generation Lexus GS was sold as the Toyota Aristo. The Aristo S300 used the same naturally aspirated 2JZ-GE as the U.S. GS 300, while the V300 packed a twin-turbo 2JZ-GTE rated at 280 PS (about 276 hp). The JZX100 Chaser Tourer V was a different car altogether, running a turbocharged 2.5-liter 1JZ-GTE. The 1998–2000 Lexus GS 400 hid serious speed behind familiar sheet metal. Its 4.0-liter 1UZ-FE V8 pumps out 300 hp and 310 lb-ft, an extra 75 hp and 90 lb-ft over the GS 300. Lexus's factory specifications put prototype 0–60 mph acceleration at 5.8 seconds, versus 7.6 for the six-cylinder. You get that speed without opening a turbo catalog. The four-cam V8 combines aluminum construction with variable valve timing to manage how its cylinders breathe. The GS 400 weighs just 55 pounds more than its six-cylinder sibling. A five-speed automatic feeds the rear wheels, while double-wishbone suspension guides them through bumps and corners. Steering-wheel E-shift buttons let you choose gears without reaching for the console. Traction control helps tame wheelspin. It's still an automatic, but Lexus gave the driver more to work with than a plain selector. The 2001 GS 430 trades 4.0 liters for 4.3 and brings 325 lb-ft at 3,400 rpm instead of the older V8's 310 at 4,000. Both make 300 hp; Lexus claimed the same 5.8-second run. If that car is better maintained, its extra torque makes it worth considering. A 300-hp Lexus V8 for $7,600? That's enough to make you check the listing twice. A 1998 GS 400 with 149,000 miles sold for that price on Bring a Trailer on June 22, 2026. Another '98, showing 48,000 miles, sold there for $12,000 on May 17. That's $4,400 extra for 101,000 fewer miles. Then inspect both. The cheaper car disclosed oil-pan and steering-rack leaks, plus a patch covering worn driver's-seat upholstery. The low-mileage one had a replacement instrument cluster calibrated to the removed unit's mileage and a faded dashboard beneath a pad. Neither was frozen in a showroom time capsule. Those winning bids also exclude buyer fees and taxes, and they aren't a market average or a guaranteed price range. Repairs can make a used Lexus bargain less charming. JDMBUYSELL reported a $15,950 Aristo median from 37 seller-reported sales dated August 2023 through October 2026, as of November 1, 2026. But those cars span generations and specifications. It's not proof of a fixed JDM premium over a GS 400. Compare cars, including fees and repairs. The GS 400 serves up luxury and muscle on the same plate: leather seats, walnut trim, dual-zone climate control, and a 300-hp V8. Before you fall for it, though, check dated receipts and mileage. Gates lists a timing-belt replacement interval of 90,000 miles or 72 months, whichever comes first. On this interference V8, a failed belt can mean pistons meeting valves, and nobody wants that introduction. Have a specialist review the belt-driven water pump, too. The S160's hydraulic brake booster, pump, accumulator, and ABS require model-specific pressure and electrical checks; warning lights or odd pump behavior deserve a repair estimate. Check stored faults, leaks, suspension wear, and the dashboard under any cover. Fading on one auction car doesn't make later-generation sticky-dashboard bulletins an S160 diagnosis. With proper maintenance and a clean inspection, this GS 400 makes a compelling used luxury sedan. But if repairs swallow the bargain, walk away. title: GS Engineering & Construction unveils 'Moving Wall' system that reshapes apartment interiors on demand - 헤럴드경제
content: Rooms and living areas can be separated or merged as needed Railless precision drive and AI management technology applied GS Engineering & Construction has unveiled a new residential product called the Moving Wall, which uses robotics technology to let apartment residents reconfigure their interior spaces as needed. The company announced the flexible space solution Tuesday, describing it as a system that allows residents to freely divide or combine rooms based on their lifestyle and intended use. The Moving Wall's defining feature is that it breaks from the fixed layout model that has long defined apartment living. Until now, buyers had to choose from a set of predetermined floor plan options at the pre-sale stage — adding a room, expanding the living area or enlarging the kitchen — and had virtually no way to change that layout after moving in. The Moving Wall lets residents shift wall panels to transform a single space for multiple purposes. Rather than choosing between a bedroom and a spacious living room, residents can have both depending on the situation — using the space as a private study or children's learning room during remote work or study sessions, then opening it up into a wide living or dining area when the family gathers. The product comes in four types tailored to different living patterns: a wide dining and alpha room type that alternates between a dining area and a separate work or study space; a hidden kitchen type that conceals the kitchen when not in use; a wide living and alpha room type that switches between a large living room and a private room; and a room-in-room type that creates a separate enclosed space within a bedroom. GS Engineering & Construction developed the underlying furniture technology in partnership with Rovothome, a robotics furniture venture backed by its subsidiary Xplor Investment. The Moving Wall uses precision drive control technology that moves the furniture unit horizontally without floor-mounted rails. The system detects and corrects lateral drift and minor misalignment in real time, allowing stable movement even in tight spaces. Low-noise, low-vibration design and obstacle and collision detection ensure safety, while an AI-based management system analyzes operational data to predict maintenance needs. Residents can control the Moving Wall's position, lighting brightness and color temperature, security and locking functions, and automated presets through a dedicated app. GS Engineering & Construction also plans to link the system with the AI Home platform it is co-developing with LG Electronics, expanding voice control capabilities and ultimately working toward a stage where the system learns residents' daily patterns and adjusts spaces automatically. The company said it intends to develop the Moving Wall — and the broader range of robotics- and AI-integrated smart flexible space solutions it represents — into a signature differentiated product for its Xi residential brand. "How efficiently and flexibly residents can use limited urban living space will become the fundamental competitive edge of apartment products going forward," a GS Engineering & Construction official said. "Through the Moving Wall, we aim to deliver a new residential value unique to Xi that residents can feel in their everyday lives." Meanwhile, GS Engineering & Construction posted consolidated sales of 2.74 trillion won ($2.05 billion) and operating profit of 95.5 billion won in the third quarter of this year.

title: GS Shop launches AI-powered 'MD curation system' to streamline merchandising - 헤럴드경제
content: Co-developed with Amazon Web Services to overhaul merchandiser workflows System cuts product selection and event preparation time by about 70% Promotion prep, which consumed 40% of MD working hours, now largely automated GS Shop has officially launched an AI-powered "MD curation system" co-developed with Amazon Web Services, the company said Tuesday, marking a push to transform how its merchandisers plan and manage promotions. The system allows merchandisers to enter a promotion's intent and conditions, after which AI analyzes sales performance and customer behavior data to recommend suitable products and support the entire process from promotion planning to registration. The tool is designed to reduce repetitive operational tasks so merchandisers can focus on higher-value work such as product sourcing and event planning. According to GS Shop, merchandisers responsible for product operations within its mobile app had been spending about 40 percent of their working hours on promotion preparation — a burden driven by the need to pull product information and sales data from multiple systems before manually selecting and arranging items. The system runs on four AI agents — product curation, store auto-mapping, trend sensing and copywriting — that together cover everything from product selection to promotion setup and registration. When a mobile merchandiser sets a promotion period, planning intent and product scope, the product curation agent draws on sales and customer behavior data to extract up to 1,000 candidate products and recommend those that best fit the brief. Merchandisers can then refine the list by conversing with the AI in natural language — for example, asking it to "pick only products suited for moisturizing, hydration and skin-barrier care." Once products are selected, the store auto-mapping agent assists with promotion layout and product placement. The trend sensing agent then analyzes internal and external data to suggest event themes, while the copywriting agent proposes event names and marketing copy, rounding out support for the full promotion planning workflow. During a month-long pilot in October, about 40 percent of all promotions were built using the new system, and the time spent on product selection and event preparation fell by roughly 70 percent compared with before. Some 72 percent of mobile merchandisers used the system during the trial period. GS Shop plans to push the system's adoption rate above 90 percent by year-end. Kim Yo-han, head of GS Retail's home shopping AI transformation division, said the project had strengthened the company's on-the-ground AI capabilities. "We will continue to spread an AI-driven work culture and translate it into tangible results," Kim said.

title: GS E&C data breach exposes blind spots in Korea's smart apartments - The Korea Times
content: GS Engineering & Construction detected unauthorized external access to a system managing apartment community-facility reservations last Wednesday. The incident has raised concerns about the security of digital services used in Korea’s apartment complexes, where residents’ personal and access-related information is collected. The full extent of the exposure remains under investigation, and experts say similar systems used by other builders and public housing operators may also warrant review. When Park, a 56-year-old homemaker living in an apartment complex in Suwon, Gyeonggi Province, heard that GS Engineering & Construction (GS E&C) had recently detected unauthorized access to a system containing residents’ personal information, the news struck a nerve. “Sure, I’ve had my personal information exposed in the Coupang and SK Telecom data breaches, among many others. Over time, I found myself becoming less concerned. Everyone seemed to be getting hit, and it felt like I was just another number in a database,” she said. This time, however, it felt much closer to home, quite literally. “The information involved could reveal details about my own household. Our apartment complex, like many newer developments, relies on smart home services for everyday tasks. We use an app to track package deliveries and vehicle entry and exit, another to access the building, and I hear the sports center is introducing facial recognition for entry. If that kind of information gets exposed, it feels like someone might actually be able to track my every move.” Her concerns point to a growing vulnerability in a country where apartment living and digital technology are increasingly intertwined. Apartments account for a staggering 65.8 percent of all homes in Korea, according to 2025 data from the Ministry of Data and Statistics. As residential complexes adopt digital systems for everything from identity verification and building access to household device controls, they are also collecting more detailed information about residents and their routines. The security implications came into focus last Wednesday, when GS E&C said it had detected unauthorized external access to a system used to manage reservations for apartment community facilities. The potentially exposed data goes beyond basic identifying details, such as residents’ names, dates of birth and contact information. It also includes information about their residential status, whether they are the head of their household and radio-frequency identification (RFID) card numbers. Passwords were also listed among the affected information, although the company said they were encrypted. The full extent of the exposure remains under investigation. A panoramic view of apartment complexes in Seoul's Seongbuk District, Sunday / Yonhap Over the years, major construction companies have expanded their digital services for residents, offering platforms that combine smart home controls with building access, visitor registration and reservations for shared facilities. GS E&C operates its “Xi Home” platform, while Hyundai Engineering & Construction, Samsung C&T and Daewoo Engineering & Construction offer similar services across their apartment complexes. As these services have proliferated, however, information security may not have kept pace with the expansion, experts say, as construction has traditionally been viewed as a building-focused sector. The risks extend beyond the exposure of personal identifiers. RFID card numbers can be linked to systems controlling access to apartment buildings and shared facilities, while some complexes are starting to use facial recognition and other biometric data for entry. “RFID cards are used to control access to apartment buildings and shared facilities like saunas and gyms,” said Youm Heung-youl, an emeritus professor of information security at Soonchunhyang University. “The risks are even greater with facial recognition. Although there is no indication that biometric information was compromised in the GS E&C incident, its exposure could create further privacy risks, including the potential misuse of facial data in AI (artificial intelligence)-generated images.” The potential impact could also extend beyond a single apartment complex. “This is unlikely to be a problem limited to GS E&C. Other construction companies and public housing operators use similar systems. If multiple apartment complexes share a platform, a breach affecting one complex could spread to others. We need to examine whether these platforms are being managed securely,” he said. The professor called for a broader review of vulnerabilities in apartment management systems and their connections to external networks, noting that existing safeguards — including certified Internet of Things devices and separation between internal and shared networks — may not be sufficient. title: Becky G might be the all-time best gift-giver — these are her top picks for this holiday season - NBC News
content: Becky G doesn’t play around with holiday gifts — here’s what she’s giving the lucky people in her life this season NBC Selected independently determines what we cover and recommend. When you click on or buy through our links, we earn a commission. Learn more. Talking Shop is our series where we talk to interesting people about their most interesting buys. Becky G has been going nonstop all year. Not only did the singer release her fifth studio album, Baraja Bendita, which was nominated for Top Latin Pop Album of the Year at the 2026 Billboard Latin Music Awards, but she also filmed a new movie and led a cross-country headlining tour. She also helped Patrón design a limited-edition “Our Rainwater Project” bottle, which funded 200 rainwater harvesting systems for households in Jalisco, Mexico. Needless to say, the L.A.-based superstar is ready for some much-needed rest and relaxation this holiday season. “I’ve been away from home a lot more this year. I’ve definitely been putting my head down and grinding it out, so I’m looking forward to family time — celebrating with them, reconnecting, and eating some yummy food,” says Becky G. “It’ll be a fun holiday, for sure.” In addition to making her family’s annual tamales, she’s preparing for Las Posadas, a nine-day religious celebration that takes place from December 16 to December 24, and readying her holiday shopping list. “I’m really big on gift giving,” she says. “It’s my favorite time of the year to catch up with everybody and give them things that I’ve put a lot of thought into.” She adds that, regardless of presents and parties, showing up and celebrating together is the most important part of the holiday season. “Now more than ever, there’s a unity that we need as a community and a time that we need with our family. It’s a beautiful reminder of what really matters in life.” Below, Becky G breaks down the gifts on her holiday shopping list this year, including a white elephant gift everyone will fight over and useful stocking stuffers. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. Becky G describes herself as ritualistic when it comes to her pre-show routines — and restocks of her go-to essentials are always appreciated around the holidays. “I always have to have palo santo and sage,” she says. “I’m really big on essence sprays and things that cleanse the space. It’s very helpful for me to set the vibes. I’m a vibe curator, so I would say those are things that I absolutely love receiving.” Lé Trois Apothecary offers three essential oil ritual cleansers: one for relaxation and release, one for manifestation, and one for grounding. The brand’s No. 3 cleanser to create unity and connection was inspired by Becky G and it features notes of bergamot, oud, and vetiver. Not one to miss her family’s white elephant gift exchange, Becky G says a bottle of Patrón Tequila was one of the best presents she’s ever brought. “It was the hot ticket item that everybody was battling it out for, and at the end, people started linking up with other people to trade gifts to get it.” An official partner of the brand, she recently designed an exclusive bottle for the Rainwater Project, which helped bring 200 rainwater harvesting systems to families in Jalisco, Mexico. A fan of buying and gifting things with intention, Becky G is planning on giving friends a bottle from that collection this year because it’s a present that’s connected to something close to her heart. “When I’ve been given things that are for the community and for the culture, it hits me differently and it reminds me that we’re a part of something bigger and it makes me want to do the same,” she says. Patrón silver tequila is an unaged blanco tequila made from 100% Weber Blue Agave. You must be 21+ to purchase and consume. If someone came up to Becky G and asked her for a mid-luxury beauty product to give as a gift, she’d recommend Dezi Skin’s Agua Fresca Moisturizer. “Desi Perkins killed it with Dezi Skin; there’s not one product that I do not love, especially Pore Choices, the new mist she just released. But, the OG Agua Fresca moisturizer is also incredible,” she says. The fragrance-free gel-cream moisturizer is formulated with niacinamide, hyaluronic acid and antioxidants to help give skin a much-needed boost of hydration. It’s lightweight and can be used with all skin types to help target fine lines, dryness and elasticity. Every year, Becky G likes to give her team presents that they can make together. Last year, she bought them a Mexican coffee set from a small cafe in Los Angeles. The kit included the coffeehouse’s signature Café de Olla — a traditional Mexican coffee brewed with ground cinnamon and piloncillo (unrefined Mexican sugar) — and a bag of Oaxaca Reserve beans. “Little thoughtful things like that are super, super fun to put together,” she says. Traditionally, café de olla is made in a clay pot, which imbues the coffee with more flavor. While you can make café de olla in a regular saucepan, you can also purchase an olla for less than $40 on Etsy — just make sure to wash it by hand with warm water and baking soda (or coarse salt) when you’re done. Chemical-based detergents are easily absorbed into the clay and can give your food (and coffee) a soapy taste. One thing about Becky G is she commits to an aesthetic. Each of her family members gets a matching color scheme for the holidays that’s themed to their personalities, which she helps curate on Etsy. “I get down on wrapping presents. That’s the one thing I enjoy,” she says, noting that she’s usually the one going around and saving the tissue paper and unripped bags. “There’s some bags that have been around at my Christmas for eight years now. We can’t just use these once, come on.” As someone who’s always traveling, Becky G loves tin candles, and she thinks they make a great addition to any stocking. “Tin candles help make a room feel a little more custom to your vibe,” she says. “They’re usually a little bit more potent in scent, so you don’t need to leave them [burning] for a very long time.” During the holidays, she opts for scents like apple cinnamon, which she says reminds her of her mom’s house, and pine. One of her go-to candle brands is Soy Latina Candles, a non-toxic soy candle brand that offers scents inspired by the owner’s Latina heritage. Another of Becky G’s go-to stocking stuffer ideas is anything practical that can be kept in a glove box, like individually packed hand wipes, silk hair ties and lip balm. “I be doing too much with the stockings sometimes. I’m like, it’s overflowing at this point,” she says. I’m a newsletter editor at NBC Selected.
